rationale_bullets: B12 Freshman of the Year returns: 78.9 PFF/464, 3,033 + 527 rush, 26 total TD at 65% and 7.8 Y/A - as a true FR who arrived in June and beat out two veterans.
The yr-2 case is structural, not hype: first actual spring in Provo, same OC (Roderick), and the two books' framing agrees ('second-year starter bonus').
Capped below elite: 8th in B12 QB Rating in 2025 and depth is 2 career snaps (Lyons on mission).
72 = top-25 unit: proven volume + elite trajectory, efficiency not yet elite.
The reigning B12 Offensive Player of the Year returns: league-high 1,305 yds, 86.3 PFF/360 - through a since-repaired shoulder injury (100 ypg after it).
The room behind him is real: Moa 79.8/49; the as-played unit sat at the 94th pctile.
82 = top-15 unit: conference's best returning skill player, minor health caveat only.

key_players.evidence: 1,305 yds (league high); PFF 86.3/360; shoulder surgery rehabbed

rationale_bullets: The lone offensive room that lost its production: all three All-B12 catchers gone - Roberts (74.5/342), TE Ryan (81.8/304) graduated, Kingston (72.6/347) expelled.
Returns are experienced but low-graded (Phillips 53.3/195, Hagen 55.3/196); the reload is pedigree - Kasper (Oregon 4*, 23 routes), W.Lyons (USC co-starter, 69.3/155), Saleapaga + 4* TE signees.
QB continuity and a proven scheme lift the floor; no proven volume target caps it. 48 = fringe-average.
Two all-league linemen return - Mitchell (1st-team All-B12 C, 77.8/923) and Gentry (69.4/796) - plus Sfarcioc (66.0/606) and Makasini (72.9/423): four returning contributors from an 80th-pctile line.
The system is the multiplier and it is attributed: OL coach Woods Top-40 in both P6 OL metrics again (#38/#18, 4% sacks); five RS-seniors in the two-deep.
Three losses (Jatta 66.1/869 the largest) and a spring-named transfer LT (Finau, 61.3/426) keep it out of the 75+ tier.
68 = top-40: elite interior anchor + proven system, LT projection.

Rotation-deep returns: retained All-B12 anchor Tanuvasa (63.2/544, 'he elevated everything'), Schoonover (69.6/455), Clegg (70.3/253), Po'uha, Akana, Purcell + Kirkland (OkSt NT) off a redshirt override.
The two best volume grades left (J.Taumoepeau 74.3/537, Lutui 69.1/537) from a 55th-pctile unit.
52 = average-plus: depth and retention real; top-end pass rush unproven.

The magazines and the tape disagree, and the caution rule sides with the tape: Uluave (#1 LB transfer, All-ACC, 100 tkl, 'All-America candidate') graded 60.5/662; Glasker ('do-it-all,' bold) graded 57.3/815; the as-played room sat at the 18th pctile.
Kelly (68.7/658, the best grade) went pro; Esera (62.0/481) returns as the third bold starter.
Production, honors, and scheme familiarity are real - the room's floor is proven starters; the grades say the ceiling is not All-America. 48 = fringe-average.

PS-backfill 2026-07-15: PS calls Uluave 4th-team All-America and the unit 'already solid... even stronger' - the THIRD independent qualitative source against the PFF-grade read. Caution-rule lean retained but softened one notch. 48 -> 50.

Two verified elite pieces return from a 92nd-pctile unit: Johnson (82.4/824, 5 INT - tied league lead) and Satuala (81.6/617; 'best safety we played all year' - opposing assistant), plus Alexander (69.6/530) and Damuni (64.6/421).
The losses are one elite starter (Wall 81.3/739, 1st-tm) + rotation (Bamba 396), and - attributed caveat - the position coach (Gilford -> Michigan).
70 = top-30: two All-B12-caliber returners + continuity, minus one star and the coach who built the #13 pass D.
A 98th-pctile SPEC unit (89.5) lost ALL THREE specialists (K Ferrin, P Vander Haar - waiver denied, LS Grimes); proxy's 99 is a pure departed-personnel artifact.
Replacements are a career-backup Sr kicker ('finally gets his chance... until 5* Laga returns from mission' - Athlon) and a true FR punter with 'mostly positive' spring reviews.
Return units (Hagen/Po'uha) and coaching continuity mitigate. 42 = below average until proven.
